shortDescription: Allows administration of Keycloak identity providers using Keycloak API

options.name: add_read_token_role_on_create
options.displayName: Add Read Token Role On Create
options.description: Enable/disable whether new users can read any stored tokens. This assigns the C(broker.read-token) role.

options.name: alias
options.description: The alias uniquely identifies an identity provider and it is also used to build the redirect URI.

options.name: auth_client_id
options.description: OpenID Connect I(client_id) to authenticate to the API with.

options.name: auth_client_secret
options.description: Client Secret to use in conjunction with I(auth_client_id) (if required).

options.name: auth_keycloak_url
options.description: URL to the Keycloak instance.

options.name: auth_password
options.description: Password to authenticate for API access with.

options.name: auth_realm
options.description: Keycloak realm name to authenticate to for API access.

options.name: auth_username
options.description: Username to authenticate for API access with.

options.name: authenticate_by_default
options.description: Specifies if this identity provider should be used by default for authentication even before displaying login screen.

options.name: config
options.description: Dict specifying the configuration options for the provider; the contents differ depending on the value of O(provider_id). Examples are given below for V(oidc) and V(saml). It is easiest to obtain valid config values by dumping an already-existing identity provider configuration through check-mode in the RV(existing) field.

options.name: connection_timeout
options.description: Controls the HTTP connections timeout period (in seconds) to Keycloak API.

options.name: display_name
options.description: Friendly name for identity provider.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Enable/disable this identity provider.

options.name: first_broker_login_flow_alias
options.description: Alias of authentication flow, which is triggered after first login with this identity provider.

options.name: hide_on_login
options.description: If hidden, login with this provider is possible only if requested explicitly, for example using the C(kc_idp_hint) parameter.

options.name: http_agent
options.description: Configures the HTTP User-Agent header.

options.name: link_only
options.description: If true, users cannot log in through this provider. They can only link to this provider. This is useful if you do not want to allow login from the provider, but want to integrate with a provider.

options.name: mappers
options.description: A list of dicts defining mappers associated with this Identity Provider.

options.name: post_broker_login_flow_alias
options.description: Alias of authentication flow, which is triggered after each login with this identity provider.

options.name: provider_id
options.description: Protocol used by this provider (supported values are V(oidc) or V(saml)).

options.name: realm
options.description: The Keycloak realm under which this identity provider resides.

options.name: refresh_token
options.description: Authentication refresh token for Keycloak API.

options.name: state
options.description: State of the identity provider. On V(present), the identity provider is created if it does not yet exist, or updated with the parameters you provide. On V(absent), the identity provider is removed if it exists.

options.name: store_token
options.description: Enable/disable whether tokens must be stored after authenticating users.

options.name: token
options.description: Authentication token for Keycloak API.

options.name: trust_email
options.description: If enabled, email provided by this provider is not verified even if verification is enabled for the realm.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Verify TLS certificates (do not disable this in production).
